old: A 1978 1 yuan from Taiwan (ROC). The obverse shows Chiang Kai-shek left; the reverse shows 壹圓; 中華民國六十七年 (ROC Year 67 = 1978), 1. Struck in copper-nickel or bronze-tone.
new: A 2008 1 yuan from Taiwan (Republic of China). The obverse shows Chiang Kai-shek facing left, with 中華民國九十七年 (Republic of China year 97, which is 2008); the reverse shows 壹圓 and 1. Struck in aluminium-bronze.
source: Record: C200 year 2008, type TW.KM.551 (Y# 551, Numista N#966 https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces966.html: 1 yuan 1981-2024, aluminium-nickel-bronze 92/6/2; the type starts in ROC year 70 = 1981). Photo C200_obv.webp reads 中華民國九十七年 (year 97 = 2008). The story said the coin is from 1978, dated 六十七年 (year 67), and 'struck in copper-nickel or bronze-tone'; year 67 is impossible for this type and contradicts both the record and the photo. Note for Claude: the type's design.text still says 六十七年 and should read 九十七年.

old: A 2010 10 centavos from Guatemala. The reverse shows Maya stela; 10 CENTAVOS, MONOLITO DE QUIRIGUA, date on arms side. Struck in cupronickel.
new: A 2010 10 centavos from Guatemala. The reverse shows Maya stela; 10 CENTAVOS, MONOLITO DE QUIRIGUA, date on arms side. Struck in stainless steel.
source: Numista N#42670 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces42670.html): Guatemala 10 centavos magnetic type 2009-2023, KM# 277.6a, stainless steel; the 2010 date exists only on this type (the copper-nickel/nickel-brass type N#2259 has no 2010 row). The story said cupronickel, copied from the record (GT.KM.277.1 composition 'cupronickel'), which is corrected to stainless steel in the pending sweep file changes_grok-bot_20261008-0002.jsonl (not merged yet). Only the metal was changed.

old: A 2016 10-cent coin from Trinidad and Tobago. The front shows the national coat of arms, held up by a scarlet ibis and a cocrico, the two national birds, with the words REPUBLIC OF TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO; the value is on the back. Struck in silver-coloured metal (the record gives copper-nickel or nickel-plated steel).
new: A 2016 10-cent coin from Trinidad and Tobago. The front shows the national coat of arms, held up by a scarlet ibis and a cocrico, the two national birds, with the words REPUBLIC OF TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO; the value is on the back. Struck in copper-nickel.
source: Record TT.KM.31 composition 'copper-nickel (KM#31, 1976-2017; the plated-steel KM#31b starts 2017)'; Numista N#3463 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces3463.html): 10 cents non-magnetic 1976-2017, KM# 31, copper-nickel. The story hedged 'silver-coloured metal (the record gives copper-nickel or nickel-plated steel)', which misstates the record. Only the metal sentence was changed.

old: A 2011 10 kuruş from Turkey. The obverse shows Atatürk portrait and state legend; the reverse shows crescent and star; large 10, KURUŞ, date, Rumi-style border. Struck in brass or CuNi-clad.
new: A 2011 10 kuruş from Turkey. The obverse shows Atatürk portrait and state legend; the reverse shows crescent and star; large 10, KURUŞ, date, Rumi-style border. Struck in nickel-brass.
source: Numista N#6165 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces6165.html): 10 kuruş 2009-2022, KM# 1241, composition nickel brass (65% Cu, 6% Ni, 29% Zn); record TR.KM.1241 'brass (nickel-brass)'. The story said 'brass or CuNi-clad'; there is no copper-nickel-clad version of this type. Only the metal was changed (design wording not re-checked on this pass).

old: A 1997 50 cents from Eritrea. The obverse shows State of Eritrea arms with a camel; the reverse shows greater kudu left; STATE OF ERITREA, 1997, 50, FIFTY CENTS. Struck in nickel-plated steel.
new: A 1997 50 cents from Eritrea. One side shows a greater kudu with the value 50; the other side shows soldiers raising the national flag, with the words LIBERTY EQUALITY JUSTICE and the year 1991. Struck in nickel-clad steel.
source: Numista N#2403 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces2403.html): Eritrea 50 cents 1997, KM# 47: obverse greater kudu, reverse five soldiers with a flag (LIBERTY EQUALITY JUSTICE, 1991); nickel clad steel. Record ER.KM.46 composition 'nickel-clad steel'. The story said one side shows the State of Eritrea arms with a camel and called the metal nickel-plated steel; neither matches the entry or the record. The legend STATE OF ERITREA / FIFTY CENTS wording was dropped because it is not in the entry's description (owner can add it back from the coin).

old: A 2015 1 dollar from Jamaica. The reverse shows arms; crocodile crest, Taino supporters, JAMAICA, ONE DOLLAR, 2015, heptagon. Struck in nickel-plated steel.
new: A 2015 1 dollar from Jamaica. The reverse shows arms; crocodile crest, Taino supporters, JAMAICA, ONE DOLLAR, 2015. The coin is round. Struck in nickel-clad steel.
source: Numista N#14369 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces14369.html): Jamaica 1 dollar round type 2008-2025, KM# 189, nickel clad steel, 3.65 g, 18.5 mm; the seven-sided (heptagonal) dollar is a different type, N#1078, 1994-2008, so a 2015 dollar is round. The story said 'heptagon' and 'nickel-plated steel'; the record's composition is corrected to nickel clad steel in the pending sweep file changes_grok-bot_20261008-0002.jsonl.
